findings.title: Semantically valid reordered offset/limit continuation is refused, hiding remaining catalog models
findings.reproducer: On a fresh CatalogIngest("openrouter"), add {data:[{id:"fixture/a"}],total_count:2,links:{next:"https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/models?limit=1000&offset=1"}}. It returns None with CONTINUATION_UNSUPPORTED and keeps only fixture/a. Identical numeric query in offset=1&limit=1000 order returns 1; adding the terminal fixture/b page then yields complete=True with both entries.
findings.violated_criterion: Architecture 5.3 line341 and Prompt A lines83-87: traverse all documented offset/limit/links/total_count pages within bounds, rejecting foreign/unknown/looping continuation. Query ordering is not a documented restriction, and this next URL has the same allowed endpoint and exact safe numeric query. Failing closed is correct for unknown endpoints/parameters but needlessly rejects this known continuation.
findings.consumer_impact: A legitimate provider continuation with the two documented query keys reversed permanently returns PARTIAL and omits later models, including a desired exact saved-entry model. Manual unverified fallback cannot supply the missing capabilities.
findings.minimum_fix: Parse continuation as data; validate exact allowlisted scheme/authority/path (or admitted relative path), exactly one offset and one limit, no extra/duplicate/blank parameters, expected numeric forward offset and limit1000. Retain loop/page/byte/deadline bounds and construct the owned request from validated numbers. Do not follow arbitrary next URLs. Add the reversed-order positive control beside the existing foreign/loop/extra-query negatives.
findings.provenance: Concrete scenario supplied by parent mid-review; independently reproduced with the current frozen production CatalogIngest. No code was changed.
